import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

Reading the tailnet memory so I can check the Mac's disk usage and the alert runbook. Mac free space fell from 119 GiB to 67 GiB over the past 15 days (about 3.5 GiB/day), so this alert reflects real growth and isn't noise. Now finding which directories are growing. Mac disk check is done: the growth comes from outside the areas my account can read, not from bob-cli. Now checking whether the garbled mail note (all the ` ` lines) is a bob-cli rendering bug. Plan scope: the disk alert itself isn't a bob-cli bug, but the garbled mail note is. Checking how mail notes get re-rendered so the plan can cover notes that are already in the vault. Writing a throwaway reproduction test with Alertmanager's email template to confirm the exact output before planning (I'll revert it afterwards). Root cause confirmed and the fix is designed. Loading the planning skill. Writing the plan. The disk alert is real, but bob-cli didn't cause it and code can't fix it. The garbled mail note behind that task is a bob-cli bug, and I've proposed a plan to fix it. **The MacDiskLow alert** - **It's a real trend, not noise.** According to athena's Prometheus, free space on the Mac's Data volume fell from 119 GiB on Nov 7 to 67 GiB today, about 3.5 GiB a day. At that rate the 15% line will keep firing. - **bob-cli isn't the cause.** Its Mac footprint is about 7.4 GiB of build output in `bob-cli/target` plus the 5.9 GiB vault. That's steady, not 50 GiB of growth. - **The growth is somewhere I can't see.** The Data volume holds about 370 GB, but my SSH user can read only about 130 GB of it (about 77 GB in your home folder). The other ~240 GB is in root-only system data, the other user accounts (`kellydonnelly`, `shelter`), or app data macOS blocks from SSH. There are no local snapshots on the Data volume holding space. - **Next step is on the Mac:** check System Settings → General → Storage, or run an elevated `du`. That's cleanup, not a code change, so it isn't in the plan. **The garbled mail note (planned)** I reproduced it with a scratch unit test using Alertmanager's email template, then reverted the test. bob's Gmail HTML renderer treats the email's source formatting as content: - Source newlines and indentation become real Markdown line breaks and ` ` lines. - Whitespace between tags becomes ` `-only paragraphs. - Mailjet's tracking links, which have no visible text, survive as empty links. Every templated HTML email hits this: alerts, CI mail, newsletters. The plan (`sase_plan_gmail_html_whitespace.md`, medium tale) makes HTML bodies follow normal browser whitespace rules: - Whitespace collapses to one space, and only `
` and block boundaries break lines. - Whitespace-only paragraphs are dropped, and so are links with no visible text. - It adds a regression test built from the Alertmanager email and a bullet in `docs/gmail.md`. It has one decision for you, `layout_rows` (default `keep_blocks`). An email's layout table usually has one content cell, and that cell keeps its separate paragraphs. Without this, fixing the whitespace would turn the whole alert into one run-on line. Notes already in the vault keep their old rendering until rebuilt. Once a release with the fix is installed on the Mac, run `bob gmail save mail/2026/261122_athena_alert_firing_macdisklow.md -R` to rebuild the alert note.
